item.title: AUR Package Dependencies
item.description:
An AUR repository supplies a PKGBUILD: executable packaging metadata, not a binary package or a dependency resolver. Building a package safely therefore requires distinguishing the dependencies that make the build possible from the dependencies installed on the resulting system.

Dependency Classes in PKGBUILD #

PKGBUILD(5) defines dependency arrays with different lifetimes:

  • depends declares packages required to run the installed package.
  • makedepends declares tools and libraries required only while building.
  • checkdepends declares packages needed by check().

Version constraints use pacman’s dependency syntax, for example depends=('libfoo>=2'). Split packages can have package-specific dependency arrays such as package_client() { depends=('libclient') }.

item.title: Maintaining AUR Packages
item.description:
The Arch User Repository stores Git repositories containing package recipes, not built packages. Maintaining an AUR package therefore means publishing a reviewable PKGBUILD and matching .SRCINFO, then validating that recipe in an isolated build environment.

Model the Package Correctly #

A PKGBUILD defines metadata such as pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, license, sources, checksums, and dependency arrays. Its functions separate stages:

  • prepare() applies patches or prepares sources.
  • build() compiles or generates software.
  • check() runs tests and requires checkdepends.
  • package() installs only below $pkgdir.

Use $srcdir for sources and build state; never write into the host filesystem from a package function. State runtime dependencies in depends, build-only tools in makedepends, and test-only packages in checkdepends. Missing declarations can remain hidden on a developer workstation and fail for users.

item.title: pacman
item.description:
pacman manages installed package records and configured Arch repositories. The local database records installed versions, reasons, files, and ownership; sync databases describe repository packages. Keep those views coherent by refreshing and upgrading in one transaction.

Inspect the Local Database #

Use -Q for installed-package queries:

sh 
pacman -Qs '^bash$'
pacman -Qi bash
pacman -Ql bash
pacman -Qo /usr/bin/pacman
pacman -Qk

-Ql lists files supplied by an installed package, -Qo finds the owner of an existing path, and -Qk checks tracked files. pacman -F instead searches the repository file database; populate it first with sudo pacman -Fy.
